especially in children, the elderly and those with pre-existing
respiratory conditions. Susceptible individuals are encouraged to
take preventative measures such as staying indoors or wearing
protective breathing masks, if outside.

properties.areaDesc: Sacramento, CA; San Joaquin, CA; Solano, CA; Yolo, CA
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 27 at 8:09AM PST until November 28 at 8:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the Sacramento River, San Joaquin
River, and other Delta waterways in Solano, Yolo, Sacramento, and
San Joaquin Counties.

* WHEN...Until 800 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 801 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.2 ft MHHW (7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri
11/27, +1.7 ft MHHW (6.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat 11/28, +1.2
ft MHHW (6.1 ft MLLW) at 4:53 PM Sun 11/29, and +0.7 ft MHHW
(5.6 ft MLLW) at 7:25 AM Mon 11/30.
* West Sacramento: +2.1 ft MHHW (6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri
11/27, +1.8 ft MHHW (6.2 ft MLLW) at 6:59 PM Sat 11/28, +1.4
ft MHHW (5.8 ft MLLW) at 8:03 PM Sun 11/29, and +1.0 ft MHHW
(5.4 ft MLLW) at 9:18 PM Mon 11/30.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27,
+7.4 ft at 6:00 PM Sat 11/28, +7.1 ft at 7:00 PM Sun 11/29,
+6.8 ft at 9:00 AM Mon 11/30, and +5.9 ft at 10:00 PM Tue
12/01.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1
properties.instruction:
Some roads that are commonly dry may become inundated during high
tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 27 at 10:57AM EST until November 27 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint Lucie and Coastal
Martin Counties.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM EST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

forecast.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 27 at 5:23AM PST until November 28 at 1:00AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and minor flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until late tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:30 AM PST Friday the stage was 17.6 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:30 AM PST Friday was 17.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue to gradually recede
and fall into minor flood stage later this morning. It will then
fall below flood stage this evening.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.6
feet on 10/20/2003.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 130 PM PST.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 27 at 7:39AM EST by NWS Grand Rapids MI
properties.description:
Areas of rain and snow will continue through mid morning, before
tapering off this afternoon. Most areas will see the rain, but
locally heavier bands will change the rain to snow. Where these bands
of snow fall, a quick accumulation of up to an inch will be possible,
mainly on grassy areas. Roads could develop a slush and become slick
temporarily, along with a quick reduction in visibility.

If drivers encounter these heavier bands of snow, slow down by laying
off the gas pedal, and leave extra room between your vehicle and
others.

properties.areaDesc: St Lawrence Island
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 27 at 3:32AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Snow and wind will be most prevalent this morning. East winds
will gust upwards of 35 mph in Gambell through 9AM and weaken
quickly thereafter. There will be lowered visibility down to 1
mile this morning. Periods of snow continue at times through
Saturday but will be lessening in intensity with gradual
improvement expected this afternoon through Saturday.

properties.areaDesc: Yukon Delta Coast
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 27 at 3:32AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Snow will increase in intensity this afternoon. Winds begin easterly
this morning but do shift to the west in the afternoon with peak
gusts upwards of 40 mph. The combination of snow and wind will
result in reduced visibility below 1 mile at times, especially
between 3PM and 10PM. Expect additional snow accumulations between 1
and 3 inches.

The steadiest snow and strongest wind will end by midnight with
improving conditions thereafter.

* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations of an inch or two.
Locally higher amounts possible over steep north facing terrain.
Winds gusting as high as 30 mph.

* WHERE...Livingston Area, Northern Park, and Paradise Valley.

* WHEN...From 8 PM this evening to noon MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slick roads and areas of reduced visibility. This
includes travel on I-90 over Bozeman Pass, where up to 5 inches of
snow is expected.
properties.instruction:
Motorists should use caution and check the latest road conditions at
5 1 1.

properties.areaDesc: Shishmaref; Bering Strait Coast; Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Interior Seward Peninsula
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 27 at 3:13AM AKST until November 28 at 9:00AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow and blowing snow expected. Total snow accumulations
between 2 and 4 inches. Winds gusting up to 40 mph.

* WHERE...Bering Strait Coast, Interior Seward Peninsula, Diomede and
Southern Seward Peninsula Coast.

* WHEN...From 3 PM this afternoon to 9 AM AKST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel may be difficult. Blowing and falling snow could
reduce visibility to 1/2 mile or less at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds peak Friday night into Saturday morning
and rapidly weaken by Saturday afternoon.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 27 at 4:03AM PST until November 27 at 1:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the Beach Hazards Statement, surf of 4 to 6 feet
with sets to 7 feed and minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 1 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM PST early
this morning. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 1 PM PST
this afternoon through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King Tides peak this morning around 7.5-7.7
feet MLLW. Surf will be falling this morning but remain elevated
into Saturday, especially for west-facing beaches. Sets up to 7
feet. Despite lower surf and waning tides, localized coastal
flooding is still likely through the Saturday morning high
tides.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.areaDesc: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 27 at 3:48AM PST until November 27 at 5:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Higher than normal astronomical tides, the King Tides,
will bring around 2.2 to 2.6 ft of inundation above ground
level in low-lying areas and shore lines during high tide
Friday.

* WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of
Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the
communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold
Beach, and Coos Bay. Also, portions of Highway 101, especially
around Coos Bay.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PST Friday. High tide on Friday is at 12:44
PM at Port Orford and 1:14 PM at Charleston. The risk of
inundation will be highest a couple hours before and after
high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying lots, parks, and roads with
some road closures expected, especially along immediate
coastlines, tidal estuaries, and sloughs. Some shoreline
erosion will occur.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 27 at 1:31AM PST until November 28 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.7 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft.

* WHERE...The Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Saturday
morning. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at
12:31 PM Friday, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM
Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM
Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Rough bar conditions expected. Seas 10 to 13 ft at 12 to
15 seconds and north winds 5 to 15 kt expected.

* WHERE...In the Main Channel of the Columbia River Bar.

* WHEN...Until 1 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft,
especially when operating near to, or attempting to cross, the
Columbia River Bar.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Ebb current of 3.46 kt at 617 AM Friday.
Seas 12 ft. Very strong ebb current of 6.75 kt at 625 PM Friday.
Seas 15 to 16 ft.
properties.instruction:
A Small Craft Advisory means that wave conditions are expected to
be hazardous to small craft in the vicinity of the Columbia River
Bar. Mariners are advised to obtain the latest bar conditions
from the United States Coast Guard before attempting to cross the
bar.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 27 at 3:00AM EST until November 27 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Pinellas, Coastal Hillsborough, Coastal Manatee,
Coastal Sarasota, Coastal Charlotte and Coastal Lee Counties.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Kent
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 27 at 2:50AM EST until November 28 at 12:00AM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...One to two feet of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Kent MD.

* WHEN...Until midnight EST tonight.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in
bayside communities and along tidal waterways. Some roads
become impassable. Minor damage to vulnerable structures may
begin to occur.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

from shore into deeper water.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 1:13PM EST by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
Rain will mix with or changeover to wet snow as temperatures quickly
drop into the lower to mid 30s this evening. The snow may become
briefly heavy overnight, allowing for minor snow accumulations above
2,000-ft elevation. A brief period of slushy conditions is possible
on high-elevation road surfaces. Valley bottoms will likely see any
minor snow accumulations confined to grassy and elevated surfaces.

If traveling over higher elevations, especially overnight, you should
expect poor visibility with periods of wet snow and slushy road
surfaces.

Snow and rain will diminish in intensity Friday before gradually
ending.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Eastern Essex; Southeast Middlesex; Suffolk; Eastern Norfolk; Eastern Plymouth; Barnstable; Dukes; Nantucket
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 12:54PM EST until November 27 at 3:00PM EST by NWS Boston/Norton MA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways (3.1 to 12.9 feet Mean Lower Low Water).

* WHERE...Eastern Essex MA, Southeast Middlesex MA, Suffolk MA,
Eastern Norfolk MA, Eastern Plymouth MA, Barnstable MA, Dukes
MA and Nantucket MA Counties.

* WHEN...From 8 AM to 3 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Shallow pockets of flooding less than one foot deep
affects the lowest lying areas along the coast, including
Morrissey Boulevard in Boston. Most roads remain passable.
Flooding up to one foot deep affects coastal roads on the
North Shore from Salem to Gloucester and Newburyport. Rough
surf will cause flooding on some coastal roads around the time
of high tide due to splashover. Roads remain passable. Low
lying areas and roads near Nantucket Harbor, including Easy
Street, may experience pockets of shallow flooding less than
one foot deep.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 26 at 4:34AM PST until November 27 at 9:27AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity for the
following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight with snow levels well above
mountain tops has driven the Skokomish River to major flood stage
this morning.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, the Skokomish River will cause major, near
record flooding throughout the Skokomish Valley. Deep and swift
flood waters will inundate residential areas, many roads including
SR 106, and much of the farm land.   Flooding will occur all along
the river including headwaters, tributaries, and other streams
within and near the Skokomish River Basin.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 AM PST Thursday the stage was 17.97 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 AM PST Thursday was 17.97 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 18.1 feet late this morning. It
will then fall below flood stage on Friday morning. Further rises
through the weekend are likely, with exceeding flood stage
possible.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 03/19/1997.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 1245 PM PST.
